scope: Physical CPU/PPU/APU execution, mapper state, PCM deterministic replay, RAM mutation boundaries and mock-DOM UI commands; not browser layout, speaker, phone or hardware acceptance.

results.name: Named checkpoints restore complete physical state without enabling history or changing the project
Checkpoint preserves mapper 1 bank state, CHR RAM, SRAM, latches and active DMC
Checkpoint preserves mapper 4 bank state, CHR RAM, SRAM, latches and active DMC
Checkpoint names and storage count are bounded without evicting another named checkpoint
Checkpoint byte bound rejects the whole save and keeps previous states intact
Unsupported live physical properties reject checkpoint restoration without partial mutation
Checkpoint restore discards incompatible frame-history future and invalidates observations
Reset, successful ROM load, CPU trace and project unload invalidate checkpoints; rejected load retains them
Input script executes native movement and reproduces the complete machine and PCM stream from a checkpoint
Scripts isolate live input and editable focus without removing unrelated blockers
Script validation is atomic for duplicate/opposite buttons, counts, addresses and stale checkpoints
Canceled scripted input stops at the yield and leaves a restorable paused checkpoint
A ROM replacement during scripted replay cancels old work before the new ROM executes
RAM experiments normalize mirrors, never call bus writers and restore the complete pre-edit machine
RAM edit rejects I/O, ROM, bad values, stale expected bytes and duplicate mirrors before mutation
Keeping a RAM experiment leaves only emulator changes and a bounded explanatory log
Public checkpoint deletion cannot discard active RAM experiment rollback, while keep and restore release it
A reset invalidates active experiment rollback instead of applying a stale session
UI exposes checkpoint/script/experiment actions, errors and literal user labels with native keyboard entry
